harvestMonths.region: Western Cape (Boland / Klein Karoo / Robertson stone-fruit areas)

evidence.quote: 7. HARVESTING OF FRUIT [...] Harvest fruit during the coolest time of day [...] Fruit should be harvested between a minimum and maximum fruit firmness of 5.5 kg and 9 kg [...] the quality of fruit coming from trees [...] Week 8 – 10 (4th week February)
evidence.doc: Culdevco (ARC/Deciduous Fruit Industry joint-venture cultivar licensing body) — African Delight® plum cultivar information; cross-referenced with Hortgro's 'TOP CULDEVCO LICENSED PLUM CULTIVARS' article

harvestMonths.notes: African Delight® (a late cultivar, 'ripens just before Angeleno®') harvests in Week 8-10 / 4th week February. Corroborating cultivar-specific harvest weeks from the same publisher (Culdevco): Flavour Star 'Week 4 (4th week January)'; Ruby Crisp 'Week 4-5 (4th week January)'. These are mid/late-season cultivars grown mainly in Boland, Klein Karoo, Robertson, Paarl, Simondium, Bonnievale, Tulbagh and the Warm Bokkeveld per the Hortgro article. Months given here [1,2] cover only the directly-quoted cultivars; the full commercial SA plum season is known to start earlier (Nov-Dec, early cultivars) but no directly-quoted primary source for those early months was captured in this session (see gaps). Editor review: months cut to [2]. The quote on this URL gives only African Delight's Week 8–10 (February); the January weeks for other cultivars come from other pages and are not in this quote.

evidence.quote: 4. FIRST HARVEST a. Trees should preferably only bear its first harvest in the third growth season. b. The first 2 years should be used for the shaping of the tree.
evidence.doc: Hortgro / Culdevco, 'TOP CULDEVCO LICENSED PLUM CULTIVARS' (2020) — African Delight® section

yearsToFirstCrop.notes: Stated for African Delight® specifically, an ARC-bred Japanese plum cultivar; 'third growth season' interpreted as year 3.

yearsToFullBearing.notes: Not explicitly given as an age. The same source gives a yield progression by orchard age instead (see yieldKgPerTreeMature notes): 3-year-old orchards 12-20 t/ha, 4-year-old orchards 20-35 t/ha, 'mature orchards' 35-50 t/ha — 'mature' age itself is not stated numerically.

evidence.quote: A yield of between 30 and 40 tons per hectare is attainable in adult orchards. [...] Tree spacing (m) 4.0 x 1.25 [...] Trees/ha 2000
evidence.doc: Hortgro / Culdevco, 'TOP CULDEVCO LICENSED PLUM CULTIVARS' (2020) — Ruby Crisp section and Table 1

yieldKgPerTreeMature.notes: CONVERTED, arithmetic shown: 'A yield of between 30 and 40 tons per hectare is attainable in adult orchards' (Ruby Crisp) combined with the spacing given in the same document's Table 1 for Ruby Crisp trial blocks ('Tree spacing (m) 4.0 x 1.25', 'Trees/ha 2000'): 4.0 x 1.25m = 5 m²/tree → 10000/5 = 2000 trees/ha (matches the table directly). 30000kg/2000 = 15 kg/tree; 40000kg/2000 = 20 kg/tree → [15,20] kg/tree. Note the source separately gives African Delight® yields as 'Mature orchards between 35 and 50 tons per hectare' but does not give African Delight's own spacing, so that figure was not converted to avoid assuming a spacing not stated for that cultivar.

evidence.quote: African Delight®: Chilling requirement: Medium to low (400 – 200 Infruitec Chilling Units). [...] Ruby Crisp: Chilling Requirement: Medium (400-600 Infruitec Chilling Units).
evidence.doc: Culdevco — African Delight® and Ruby Crisp plum cultivar information sheets

chillUnits.notes: Range spans the lowest (African Delight, 200 CU) to highest (Flavour Star, 'Medium (500-600 Infruitec Chilling Units)' per its own Culdevco sheet) Infruitec Chilling Unit figures found among the five ARC-bred cultivars documented in the Hortgro/Culdevco article. Not a single-cultivar figure but a range across cultivars grown in South Africa.

evidence.quote: 2. CROSS POLLINATION a. African Rose® is recommended as a cross-pollinator for most areas in South Africa at a 10% ratio. Where Pioneer is already used as a cross-pollinator it is not necessary to use African Rose®. b. Bees should be used in orchards to optimise the pollination process.
evidence.doc: Hortgro / Culdevco, 'TOP CULDEVCO LICENSED PLUM CULTIVARS' (2020) — African Delight® section

pollination.notes: Consistent across all five ARC-bred Japanese plum cultivars documented in this source: Flavour Star needs 'Laetitia and Larry Ann' plus 'Songold' as pollinators ('It is recommended to plant both pollinators'); Ruby Crisp needs 'Harry Pickstone and Fortune ... as cross pollinators ... at a ratio of 10%'; Ruby Sun needs 'Harry Pickstone ... as a cross pollinator ... at a ratio of 10% to 15%'; Ruby Star needs 'Songold, Southern Belle, or both ... as cross pollinators ... in a 10% ratio'. This strongly and consistently supports 'needs-cross-pollinator' for commercial Japanese plum cultivars grown in South Africa (as opposed to a generic species-level claim; some plum cultivars elsewhere are self-fertile, but the SA commercial cultivars documented here are not).

gaps: Only mid/late-season cultivar harvest weeks (Jan-Feb) were directly quoted; early-season SA plum cultivars (e.g. Sapphire, Songold, Laetitia) reportedly harvest earlier (Nov-Dec) per unquoted search summaries, but no primary source with a verbatim quote for those months was captured in this session, so the full-season range is likely wider than [1,2] — recorded as a gap rather than guessed.
'Years to full bearing' (as a specific age, distinct from an orchard-age yield table) not found.

Yield-per-tree required combining a yield range and a spacing figure that both appear in the same source but for the same cultivar (Ruby Crisp) rather than as a single explicit per-tree statement — treat [15,20] kg/tree as a derived approximation.

A ScienceDirect peer-reviewed paper ('Chilling and heat requirements of Japanese plum cultivars for flowering') was found via search and looked highly relevant (reportedly covering cultivars from 'Pioneer' at 334.3 CU to 'Songold' at 987.5 CU) but could not be fetched (403 Forbidden) in this session, so its figures were not used as they could not be verified against a verbatim quote.
DALRRD/nda.gov.za and ARC-Infruitec-Nietvoorbij's own (as opposed to Culdevco/Hortgro-hosted) plum production guidelines were not directly reachable.
Editor review 2026-09-28: harvest window cut from Jan–Feb to Feb, which is all the quoted African Delight sheet supports.
